ports.note: Two tables in, one out: the rows of the second under the first, columns lined up by name. Both must have the same value column and unit; a key column only one has is empty on the other's rows.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet. The receipt names how many rows came from each table and every column only one of them has.

changes.description: On the standard Inspector and dialog (experiment 186), changed the same day and so moved, as every widget touched is: the Inspector says in one sentence what is stacked; the tables, the source column and its labels, whether they are numbers, and a new key are set in Configure…, with the stacked table as the preview, and nothing changes until Apply.

evidence.note: Unit tested on columns both, one and neither table hold, different value columns and units, and a source column that clashes. The Salmonella example uses it to stack 32 cases on 81 matched panel controls. Nothing here establishes that two tables are fit to be stacked. 0.2.1: tests/append-rows.test.mjs; tests/population-example-opens.browser.mjs; Chromium. 0.2.2: tests/salmonella-from-scratch.browser.mjs (the matched panel controls appended through the dialog, the sentence naming both labels); Chromium.
